title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 89 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 489–491 (Night 89, continuing directly from nights-88), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 89 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Recalling the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī’s counsel, the night follows the Christian plan to land fifty thousand men at the Mountain of Smoke, then the great battle at the seashore in which Sharrukān and Ḍawʾ al-Makān win the day, and ends with King Afrīdūn announcing his champion Lūqā and the “Greatest Incense” of the patriarch, before dawn cuts Shahrazād off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ التَّاسِعَةُ وَالثَّمَانُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-tāsiʿatu wa-al-thamānūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the ninth and the eighty,
sentences.i: And when it was the eighty-ninth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ هَذَا كُلَّهُ كَانَ بِتَدْبِيرِ الْعَجُوزِ لِأَنَّ الْمَلِكَ كَانَ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهَا قَبْلَ خُرُوجِهِ وَقَالَ لَهَا كَيْفَ الْعَمَلُ وَالتَّدْبِيرُ وَأَنْتِ السَّبَبُ فِي هَذَا الْأَمْرِ الْعَسِيرِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdaanna hādhā kullahu kāna bi-tadbīri al-ʿajūzi li-anna al-malika kāna aqbala ʿalayhā qabla khurūjihi wa-qāla lahā kayfa al-ʿamalu wa-al-tadbīru wa-anti al-sababu fī hādhā al-amri al-ʿasīri
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that all of this was by the contrivance of the old woman, because the king had turned to her before his going out, and said to her: How is the doing and the contriving, and you are the cause in this hard affair?
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that all this was by the old woman’s scheming: before he set out the king had turned to her and said, “What are we to do, and how are we to plan? You are the cause of this hard business.”
sentences.n: The night opens by recalling the end of the last one. The print runs أن (“that”) into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); it is read as two words, and the spacing is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ الْكَبِيرُ وَالْكَاهِنُ الْخَطِيرُأَنِّي أُشِيرُ عَلَيْكَ بِأَمْرٍ يَعْجِزُ عَنْ تَدْبِيرِهِ إِبْلِيسُ وَلَوِ اسْتَعَانَ عَلَيْهِ بِحِزْبِهِ الْمَتَاعِيسِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku al-kabīru wa-al-kāhinu al-khaṭīruannī ushīru ʿalayka bi-amrin yaʿjizu ʿan tadbīrihi iblīsu wa-law istaʿāna ʿalayhi bi-ḥizbihi al-matāʿīsi
sentences.l: And she said: Know, O king the great and priest the weighty, that I counsel you with a matter that Iblīs is unable to contrive, even if he sought help against it with his party, the wretched ones.
sentences.i: She said: “Know, great king and mighty priest, that I advise you to a plan that even Iblīs could not devise, though he called on his whole wretched party to help him.”
sentences.n: The print runs الخطير and اني together (الخطيراني); the spacing is kept as printed. Iblīs is the devil; “his party” are his demons. The old woman addresses the king of Rūm as both king and priest.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ أَنَّكَ تُرْسِلُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفًا مِنَ الرِّجَالِ يَنْزِلُونَ فِي الْمَرَاكِبِ وَيَتَوَجَّهُونَ فِي الْبَحْرِ إِلَى أَنْ يَصِلُوا إِلَى جَبَلِ الدُّخَانِ وَيُقِيمُونَ هُنَاكَ وَلَايَرْحَلُونَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْمَكَانِ حَتَّى تَأْتِيَكُمْ أَعْلَامُ الْإِسْلَامِ فَدُونَكُمْ وَإِيَّاهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-huwa annaka tursilu khamsīna alfan mina al-rijāli yanzilūna fī al-marākibi wa-yatawajjahūna fī al-baḥri ilā an yaṣilū ilā jabali al-dukhāni wa-yuqīmūna hunāka wa-lāyarḥalūna min dhālika al-makāni ḥattā ta’tiyakum aʿlāmu al-islāmi fa-dūnakum wa-iyyāhum
sentences.l: And it is that you send fifty thousand of men, who go down into the ships and head out on the sea until they reach the Mountain of Smoke, and stay there and do not depart from that place until the banners of Islam come to you; then, upon you and them!
sentences.i: It is this: send fifty thousand men down to the ships and out over the sea until they reach the Mountain of Smoke. Let them stay there, and not leave that place until the banners of Islam come up to you. Then the field is yours, and theirs.
sentences.n: فدونكم وإياهم is a call to engage: “there you are, and they!” — the moment to fall on the enemy. The print joins لا to the verb (ولايرحلون); the spacing is kept as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَخْرُجُ إِلَيْهِمُ الْعَسَاكِرُ مِنَ الْبَحْرِ وَيَكُونُونَ خَلْفَهُمْ وَنَحْنُ نُقَابِلُهُمْ مِنَ الْبَرِّ فَلَا يَنْجُو مِنْهُمْ أَحَدٌ وَقَدْ زَالَ عَنَّا الْعَنَاءُ وَدَامَ لَنَا الْهَنَاءُ
sentences.tr: thumma takhruju ilayhimu al-ʿasākiru mina al-baḥri wa-yakūnūna khalfahum wa-naḥnu nuqābiluhum mina al-barri fa-lā yanjū minhum aḥadun wa-qad zāla ʿannā al-ʿanāʾu wa-dāma lanā al-hanāʾu
sentences.l: Then the armies come out to them from the sea and are behind them, and we meet them from the land, so none of them escapes; and the toil has gone from us, and the gladness has lasted for us.
sentences.i: Then the troops come out against them from the sea and fall on their rear, while we meet them from the land, and not one of them escapes. Our toil will be over, and our happiness will last.
sentences.n: The rhyme ʿanāʾ / hanāʾ (“toil / gladness”) is the old woman’s sajʿ.

sentences.t: فَاسْتَصْوَبَ الْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ كَلَامَ الْعَجُوزِ وَقَالَ نِعْمَ الرَّأْيُ رَأْيُكِ يَاسَيِّدَةَ الْعَجَائِزِ الْمَاكِرَةِ وَمَرْجِعَ الْكُهَّانِ فِى الْفِتَنِ الثَّائِرَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-astawwaba al-maliku afrīdūnu kalāma al-ʿajūzi wa-qāla niʿma al-raʾyu raʾyuki yāsayyidata al-ʿajāʾizi al-mākirati wa-marjiʿa al-kuhhāni fī al-fitani al-thāʾirati
sentences.l: And the king Afrīdūn judged the old woman’s speech right, and said: Excellent is the opinion, your opinion, O lady of the old women, the crafty, and resort of the priests in the rising troubles.
sentences.i: King Afrīdūn judged the old woman’s words sound, and said, “Excellent is the plan, and it is yours, O mistress of crafty old women, refuge of the priests in every rising strife!”
sentences.n: The print joins يا to the next word (ياسيدة); the spacing is kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَحِينَ هَجَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَسْكَرُ الْإِسْلَامِ فِى ذَلِكَ الْوَادِي لَمْ يَشْعُرُوا إِلَّا وَالنَّارُ تَلْتَهِبُ فِي الْخِيَامِ وَالسُّيُوفُ تَعْمَلُ فِى الْأَجْسَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥīna hajama ʿalayhim ʿaskaru al-islāmi fī dhālika al-wādī lam yashʿurū illā wa-al-nāru taltahibu fī al-khiyāmi wa-al-suyūfu taʿmalu fī al-ajsāmi
sentences.l: And when the army of Islam fell upon them in that valley, they were not aware but that the fire was blazing in the tents and the swords were working in the bodies.
sentences.i: When the army of Islam fell upon them in that valley, they knew nothing until the fire was blazing in the tents and the swords were at work on their bodies.
sentences.n: The print points a shadda on الّا; it is kept.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَتْ جُيُوشُ بَغْدَادَ وَخُرَاسَانَ وَهُمْ فِي مِائَةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ فَارِسٍ وَفِي أَوَائِلِهِمْ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbalat juyūshu baghdāda wa-khurāsāna wa-hum fī miʾatin wa-ʿishrīna alfa fārisin wa-fī awāʾilihim ḍawʾu al-makāni
sentences.l: Then the armies of Baghdad and Khurāsān came on, and they in a hundred and twenty thousand horsemen, and in their first ranks Ḍawʾ al-Makān.
sentences.i: Then the armies of Baghdad and Khurāsān came on, a hundred and twenty thousand horsemen, with Ḍawʾ al-Makān in the van.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُمْ عَسْكَرُ الْكُفَّارِ الَّذِينَ كَانُوا فِي الْبَحْرِ طَلَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ مِنَ الْبَحْرِ وَتَبِعُوا أَثَرَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhum ʿaskaru al-kuffāri alladhīna kānū fī al-baḥri ṭalaʿū ilayhim mina al-baḥri wa-tabiʿū athrahum
sentences.l: And when the army of the unbelievers who had been in the sea saw them, they came up to them from the sea and followed their track.
sentences.i: When the unbelievers’ troops who had been in the sea saw them, they came up out of the sea and followed on their tracks.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُمْ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ قَالَ ارْجِعُوا إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ يَاحِزْبَ النَّبِيِّ الْمُخْتَارِ وَقَاتِلُوا أَهْلَ الْكُفْرِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ فِي طَاعَةِ الرَّحِيمِ الرَّحْمَنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhum ḍawʾu al-makāni qāla irjiʿū ilā al-kuffāri yāḥizba al-nabiyyi al-mukhtāri wa-qātilū ahla al-kufri wa-al-ʿudwāni fī ṭāʿati al-raḥīmi al-raḥmāni
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw them he said: Return to the unbelievers, O party of the Prophet, the chosen, and fight the people of unbelief and enmity in obedience to the Merciful, the Compassionate.
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw them he cried, “Turn back upon the unbelievers, party of the chosen Prophet, and fight the people of unbelief and aggression in obedience to the Merciful, the Compassionate!”
sentences.n: The print joins يا to the next word (ياحزب); the spacing is kept as printed. “Return to the unbelievers” means turn and face them, since they have come up from behind.

sentences.t: وَأَقْبَلَ شَرْكَانُ بِطَائِفَةٍ أُخْرَى مِنْ عَسَاكِرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ نَحْوَ مِائَةِ أَلْفٍ وَعِشْرِينَ أَلْفًا وَكَانَتْ عَسَاكِرُ الْكُفَّارِ نَحْوَ أَلْفِ أَلْفٍ وَسِتِّمِائَةِ أَلْفٍ
sentences.tr: wa-aqbala sharrukānu bi-ṭāʾifatin ukhrā min ʿasākiri al-muslimīna naḥwa miʾati alfin wa-ʿishrīna alfan wa-kānat ʿasākiru al-kuffāri naḥwa alfi alfin wa-sittimiʾati alfin
sentences.l: And Sharrukān came on with another band of the armies of the Muslims, about a hundred thousand and twenty thousand; and the armies of the unbelievers were about a thousand thousand and six hundred thousand.
sentences.i: Sharrukān came on with another body of the Muslim troops, some hundred and twenty thousand, while the unbelievers’ armies numbered about one million six hundred thousand.
sentences.n: The numbers are the narrator’s own, and are meant to astonish rather than to be counted.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اخْتَلَطَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ بَعْضُهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ قَوِيَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَنَادَوْا قَائِلِينَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَعَدَنَا بِالنَّصْرِ وَأَوْعَدَ الْكُفَّارَ بِالْخِذْلَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ikhtalaṭa al-muslimūna baʿḍuhum bi-baʿḍin qawiyat qulūbuhum wa-nādaw qāʾilīna inna allāha waʿadanā bi-al-naṣri wa-awʿada al-kuffāra bi-al-khidhlāni
sentences.l: And when the Muslims mingled, some of them with others, their hearts grew strong, and they called out, saying: Truly God has promised us victory, and has threatened the unbelievers with abandonment.
sentences.i: When the two Muslim bodies joined, each with the other, their hearts took strength, and they cried out, “God has promised us victory, and has threatened the unbelievers with desertion!”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَصَادَمُوا بِالسَّيْفِ وَالسِّنَانِ وَاخْتَرَقَ شَرْكَانُ الصُّفُوفَ وَهَاجَ فِي الْأُلُوفِ وَقَاتَلَ قِتَالًا تَشِيبُ مِنْهُ الْأَطْفَالُ
sentences.tr: thumma taṣādamū bi-al-sayfi wa-al-sinān-i wa-ikhtaraqa sharrukānu al-ṣufūfa wa-hāja fī al-ulūfi wa-qātala qitālan tashību minhu al-aṭfālu
sentences.l: Then they clashed with the sword and the spear-point, and Sharrukān pierced the ranks, and raged among the thousands, and fought a fighting at which children turn grey.
sentences.i: Then they clashed with sword and spear. Sharrukān cut through the ranks and raged among the thousands, and fought so that children would turn grey at the sight.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَجُولُ فِي الْكُفَّارِ وَيَعْمَلُ فِيهِمُ الصَّارِمَ الْبَتَّارَ وَيُنَادِي اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ حَتَّى رَدَّ الْقَوْمَ إِلَى سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ وَكَلَّتْ مِنْهُمُ الْأَجْسَامُ وَنَصَرَ اللَّهُ دِينَ الْإِسْلَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal yajūlu fī al-kuffāri wa-yaʿmalu fīhimu al-ṣārima al-battāra wa-yunādī allāhu akbaru ḥattā radda al-qawma ilā sāḥili al-baḥri wa-kallat minhumu al-ajsāmu wa-naṣara allāhu dīna al-islāmi
sentences.l: And he did not cease to range among the unbelievers and to ply among them the keen, the cutting sword, and to call out: God is greatest, until he drove the people back to the shore of the sea, and the bodies of them grew weary, and God gave victory to the religion of Islam.
sentences.i: He never ceased ranging among the unbelievers, plying the keen, cutting sword among them and crying “God is greatest!”, until he drove them back to the seashore. Their bodies wearied, and God gave victory to the faith of Islam.

sentences.t: وَالنَّاسُ يُقَاتِلُونَ وَهُمْ سُكَارَى بِغَيْرِ مُدَامٍ وَقَدْ قُتِلَ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ فِي هَذِهِ الْوَقْعَةِ خَمْسَةٌ وَأَرْبَعُونَ أَلْفًا وَقُتِلَ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ ثَلٰثَةُ آلَافٍ وَخَمْسُمِائَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-al-nāsu yuqātilūna wa-hum sukārā bi-ghayri mudāmin wa-qad qutila mina al-kuffāri fī hādhihi al-waqʿati khamsatun wa-arbaʿūna alfan wa-qutila mina al-muslimīna thalāthatu ālāfin wa-khamsumiʾatin
sentences.l: And the people were fighting, and they drunk without wine; and there were killed of the unbelievers in this battle forty-five thousand, and there were killed of the Muslims three thousand and five hundred.
sentences.i: The men fought as if drunk, though without wine. In that battle forty-five thousand of the unbelievers were killed, and three thousand five hundred of the Muslims.
sentences.n: The print spells ثلثة without the long alif; it is vocalised ثَلٰثَةُ, with the dagger alif.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ أَسَدَالدِّينِ الْمَلِكَ شَرْكَانَ لَمْ يَنَمْ فِي تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةِ لَاهُوَ وَلَا أَخُوهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ بَلْ كَانَا يُبَشِّرَانِ النَّاسَ وَيَتَفَقَّدَانِ الْجَرْحَى وَيُهَنِّئَانِهِمْ بِالنَّصْرِ وَالسَّلَامَةِ وَالثَّوَابِ فِي الْقِيَامَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna asadaldīni al-malika sharrukāna lam yanam fī tilka al-laylati lāhuwa wa-lā akhūhu ḍawʾu al-makāni bal kānā yubashshirāni al-nāsa wa-yatafaqqadāni al-jarḥā wa-yuhanniʾānihim bi-al-naṣri wa-al-salāmati wa-al-thawābi fī al-qiyāmati
sentences.l: Then Asad al-Dīn, the king Sharrukān, did not sleep that night, neither he nor his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, but they were giving the people glad tidings, and looking in on the wounded, and congratulating them on the victory, and the safety, and the reward in the Resurrection.
sentences.i: That night Asad al-Dīn, King Sharrukān, did not sleep, nor did his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān; they went among the men with glad tidings and looked in on the wounded, congratulating them on the victory, on their safety, and on the reward awaiting them at the Resurrection.
sentences.n: The print has اخوة, a misprint for اخوه (“his brother”), corrected here. Asad al-Dīn (“lion of the faith”) is Sharrukān’s title; the print joins the two words (اسدالدين) and also لاهو, and the spacing is kept as printed.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَأَمَّا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ مَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ وَمَلِكِ الرُّومِ وَأُمِّهِ الْعَجُوزِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي فَإِنَّهُمْ جَمَعُوا أُمَرَاءَ الْعَسْكَرِ وَقَالُوا لِبَعْضِهِمْ إِنَّا كُنَّا بَلَغْنَا الْمُرَادَ وَشَفَيْنَا الْفُؤَادَ وَلَكِنْ إِعْجَابَنَا بِكَثْرَتِنَا هُوَ الَّذِي خَذَلَنَا
sentences.tr: hādhā mākāna min amri al-muslimīna wa-ammā mākāna min amri al-maliki afrīdūna maliki al-quṣṭanṭīniyyati wa-maliki al-rūmi wa-ummihi al-ʿajūzi dhāti al-dawāhī fa-innahum jamaʿū umarāʾa al-ʿaskari wa-qālū li-baʿḍihim innā kunnā balaghnā al-murāda wa-shafaynā al-fuʾāda wa-lākin iʿjābanā bi-kathratinā huwa alladhī khadhalanā
sentences.l: This was what was of the affair of the Muslims. And as for what was of the affair of the king Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople and king of Rūm, and his mother the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī, they gathered the emirs of the army and said to one another: We had reached the aim and healed the heart, but our wonder at our numbers is what forsook us.
sentences.i: So much for the Muslims. As for King Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople and of Rūm, and his mother, the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī, they gathered the emirs of the army and said to one another, “We had reached our goal and slaked our hearts, but it is our pride in our numbers that has undone us.”
sentences.n: The print joins ما to كان (ماكان); the spacing is kept as printed. “Healed the heart”: satisfied the thirst for vengeance.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُمُ الْعَجُوزُ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي إِنَّهُ لَايَنْفَعُكُمْ إِلَّا أَنَّكُمْ تَتَقَرَّبُوا لِلْمَسِيحِ وَتَتَمَسَّكُوا بِالِاعْتِقَادِ الصَّحِيحِ فَوَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ مَا قَوَّى عَسْكَرَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِلَّا هَذَا الشَّيْطَانُ الْمَلِكُ شَرْكَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahumu al-ʿajūzu dhātu al-dawāhī innahu lāyanfaʿukum illā annakum tataqarrabū li-al-masīḥi wa-tatamassakū bi-al-iʿtiqādi al-ṣaḥīḥi fa-wa-ḥaqqi al-masīḥi mā qawwā ʿaskara al-muslimīna illā hādhā al-shayṭānu al-maliku sharrukānu
sentences.l: And the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī said to them: Nothing will profit you except that you draw near to the Messiah and hold fast to the sound belief; for by the right of the Messiah, nothing strengthened the army of the Muslims but this devil, the king Sharrukān.
sentences.i: Then the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī said to them, “Nothing will serve you but to draw near to the Messiah and hold fast to the true faith. By the Messiah’s right, nothing has strengthened the Muslim army but that devil, King Sharrukān!”
sentences.n: The print gives تتقربوا and تتمسكوا without the final nūn, as if after أن, though it follows انكم; it is kept as printed and vocalised as subjunctives. The print joins لا to the verb (لاينفعكم) and و to حق (فوحق).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ إِنِّي قَدْ عَوَّلْتُ فِي غَدٍ عَلَى أَنْ أَصُفَّ لَهُمُ الصُّفُوفَ وَأُخْرِجَ لَهُمُ الْفَارِسَ الْمَعْرُوفَ لُوقَا بْنَ شَمْلُوطٍ فَإِنَّهُ إِذَا بَرَزَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ شَرْكَانَ قَتَلَهُ وَقَتَلَ غَيْرَهُ مِنَ الْأَبْطَالِ حَتَّى لَمْ يَبْقَ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدٌ وَقَدْ عَوَّلْتُ فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ عَلَى تَقْدِيسِكُمْ بِالْبَخُورِ الْأَكْبَرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku afrīdūnu innī qad ʿawwaltu fī ghadin ʿalā an aṣuffa lahumu al-ṣufūfa wa-ukhrija lahumu al-fārisa al-maʿrūfa lūqā bna shamlūṭin fa-innahu idhā baraza ilā al-maliki sharrukāna qatalahu wa-qatala ghayrahu mina al-abṭāli ḥattā lam yabqa minhum aḥadun wa-qad ʿawwaltu fī hādhihi al-laylati ʿalā taqdīsikum bi-al-bakhūri al-akbari
sentences.l: And the king Afrīdūn said: I have relied for tomorrow on setting the ranks in array for them, and bringing out to them the well-known horseman Lūqā son of Shamlūṭ; for when he comes out to the king Sharrukān he will kill him, and kill others of the heroes, until none of them is left. And I have relied this night on hallowing you with the greatest incense.
sentences.i: King Afrīdūn said, “I have resolved that tomorrow I shall draw up the ranks against them and bring out the renowned horseman Lūqā son of Shamlūṭ. When he goes out against King Sharrukān he will kill him, and other heroes besides, until not one of them is left. And tonight I have resolved to hallow you with the Greatest Incense.”

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعُوا كَلَامَهُ قَبَّلُوا الْأَرْضَ وَكَانَ الْبَخُورُ الَّذِي أَرَادَهُ خُرْءَ الْبَطْرِيقِ الْكَبِيرِ ذِي الْإِنْكَارِ وَالنَّكِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿū kalāmahu qabbalū al-arḍa wa-kāna al-bakhūru alladhī arādahu khurʾa al-baṭrīqi al-kabīri dhī al-inkāri wa-al-nakīri
sentences.l: And when they heard his speech they kissed the ground; and the incense that he meant was the dung of the great patriarch, possessor of the denial and the rebuke.
sentences.i: When they heard his words they kissed the ground. The incense he meant was the dung of the Great Patriarch, he of the stern denunciations.
sentences.n: The Christians’ “incense” is the patriarch’s excrement, which the narrator, in the same vein as the rest of the passage, describes as a prized relic. This is the text’s own mockery of the Christians; it is translated as printed. “Denial and rebuke” is a pair of rhyming words for his censure.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يَتَنَافَسُونَ فِيهِ وَيَسْتَحْسِنُونَ مَسَاوِيَهُ حَتَّى كَانَتْ أَكَابِرُ بَطَارِقَةِ الرُّومِ يَبْعَثُونَهُ إِلَى سَائِرِ أَقَالِيمِ بِلَادِهِمْ فِي خِرَقٍ مِنَ الْحَرِيرِ وَيَمْزُجُونَهُ بِالْمِسْكِ وَالْعَبِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-innahum kānū yatanāfasūna fīhi wa-yastaḥsinūna masāwiyahu ḥattā kānat akābiru baṭāriqati al-rūmi yabʿathūnahu ilā sāʾiri aqālīmi bilādihim fī khiraqin mina al-ḥarīri wa-yamzujūnahu bi-al-miski wa-al-ʿabīri
sentences.l: For they used to vie for it and to think its foulnesses fair, so that the greatest of the patriarchs of Rūm would send it to all the regions of their land in rags of silk, and mix it with musk and ambergris.
sentences.i: They would vie for it and think its very foulness fine, so that the greatest patriarchs of Rūm sent it to every province of their country wrapped in scraps of silk, and mixed it with musk and perfume.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا وَصَلَ خَبَرُهُ إِلَى الْمُلُوكِ يَأْخُذُونَ مِنْهُ كُلَّ دِرْهَمٍ بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ حَتَّى كَانَ الْمُلُوكُ يُرْسِلُونَ فِى طَلَبِهِ مِنْ أَجْلِ بَخُورِ الْعَرَائِسِ وَكَانَتِ الْبَطَارِقَةُ يَخْلِطُونَهُ بِخُرْئِهِمْ فَإِنَّ خُرْءَ الْبَطْرِيقِ الْكَبِيرِ لَايَكْفِي عَشَرَةَ أَقَالِيمَ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā waṣala khabaruhu ilā al-mulūki yaʾkhudhūna minhu kulla dirhamin bi-alfi dīnārin ḥattā kāna al-mulūku yursilūna fī ṭalabihi min ajli bakhūri al-ʿarāʾisi wa-kānati al-baṭāriqatu yakhliṭūnahu bi-khurʾihim fa-inna khurʾa al-baṭrīqi al-kabīri lāyakfī ʿasharata aqālīma
sentences.l: And when news of it reached the kings they would take of it each dirham at a thousand dinars, so that the kings used to send in search of it, for the incense of brides; and the patriarchs used to mix it with their own dung, for the dung of the great patriarch does not suffice for ten regions.
sentences.i: When word of it reached the kings they would pay a thousand dinars for every dirham’s weight, and sent seeking it out for the incense of brides. The patriarchs therefore mixed it with their own dung, since the Great Patriarch’s alone would not suffice for ten provinces.
sentences.n: The print joins لا to the verb (لايكفي); the spacing is kept as printed. A dirham is a small unit of weight, about three grams.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ خَوَاصُّ مُلُوكِهِمْ يَجْعَلُونَ قَلِيلًا مِنْهُ فِي كُحْلِ الْعُيُونِ وَيُدَاوُونَ بِهِ الْمَرِيضَ وَالْمَبْطُونَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna khawāṣṣu mulūkihim yajʿalūna qalīlan minhu fī kuḥli al-ʿuyūni wa-yudāwūna bihi al-marīḍa wa-al-mabṭūna
sentences.l: And the intimates of their kings used to put a little of it in the kohl of the eyes, and to treat with it the sick and the one with the belly.
sentences.i: The favourites among their kings put a little of it in their eye-salve, and treated the sick and those with bowel complaints with it.
sentences.n: المبطون is one suffering in the belly, that is, from a bowel disorder.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ وَأَشْرَقَ بِنُورِهِ وَلَاحَ وَتَبَادَرَتِ الْفُرْسَانُ إِلَى حَمْلِ الرِّمَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu wa-ashraqa bi-nūrihi wa-lāḥa wa-tabādarati al-fursānu ilā ḥamli al-rimāḥi
sentences.l: And when the morning dawned, and shone with its light, and appeared, and the horsemen hastened to the bearing of the lances,
sentences.i: When morning dawned, shone with its light and spread, and the horsemen hastened to take up their lances,

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُ—بَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahra zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as in every night; the print splits the name into شهر and زاد and breaks the last word with a dash.
